clue.text: Using free ticket, others picked up song that could be Under Pressure

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by the ear, so the words are taken by their sound rather than their spelling

blocks.note: to be comped is to be given a free ticket, and the others are the rest; said together they sound like a word for squeezed
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A fan on a free ticket hears the rest of the crowd join in with Queen's Under Pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Under Pressure is the Queen and David Bowie song, which keeps the musical surface going while the def reads literally: air held under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Compressed air is literally gas kept at high pressure, as in a tyre or a diver's tank.

clue.text: Working prior to article in which dancers appear alert

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on
the definite article
a ball is a formal dance where dancers gather

explanation.surface: A dancer at work before a newspaper piece about a dance troupe looks sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior to' simply places the first piece ahead of the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball is an idiom for being quick-witted and attentive.

clue.text: Pinch little dog with half-docked tail

blocks.note: a pug is a small snub-nosed dog breed
taken as written, before half is cut away

explanation.surface: A small dog with a half-cropped tail gets a pinch.
explanation.walkthrough: Docking removes the front half here, not the tip. The answer is a rare word for as much as can be held between finger and thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugil is an old measure: the small quantity taken up between the thumb and two fingers, much like a pinch.

clue.text: Just cut doubles on court and play off and on

indicators.note: to double back is to turn round and retrace your path, so the word before runs the other way
switching off and on alternately means every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to axe something is to cut it

the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tennis report: a player cuts a doubles shot on court, then plays on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis words court and doubles hide their jobs: 'doubles' means turns back, and 'on' places the reversed cut ahead of the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adverb means precisely, as in 'just right', which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Force engineers over supporting school planner

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the letters of the engineers' name run backwards
in a down entry a supporting piece sits below the one it holds up, so it comes second

blocks.note: SCH is a common abbreviation for school
REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers are posted to back up a school's planning team.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is a corps of the British Army, hence 'Force engineers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A schemer is someone who plots or devises plans, often crafty ones.

clue.text: Articulate doctor checks shopper

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back, so the outer word holds the other in its grip

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
to enounce is to articulate or pronounce clearly

explanation.surface: A well-spoken doctor inspects a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopper' is not a customer: in British slang to shop someone is to inform on them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A denouncer publicly accuses someone, and a shopper in slang is an informer who betrays another to the authorities.

clue.text: One sod of course forgetting verse in Dumbo

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out, so a letter drops from the word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a divot is a piece of turf gouged out on a golf course
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A golfer's clod of turf loses a verse in the Disney film about a flying elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sod' looks like an insult, but here it is a piece of turf, and 'of course' means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is informal for a stupid person, a synonym for a fool or nitwit.

clue.text: Team players act with calm, mainly working out

working something out involves rearranging it, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.walkthrough: CALM loses its last letter before joining the mix. Crystal Palace is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal Palace is an English football club based in south London, so it is an example of a team.

clue.text: Press sent Queen brief solemn final letter to 'ER'

indicators.note: sent can mean carried away or transported, so the letters are thrown into a new order
a brief version is cut short, so the word loses its last letter
to here means attached against, so the pieces are joined in sequence

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, before trimming
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: The newspapers dispatch a grave last letter from the monarch to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers, but it is a device for pressing; ER, Elizabeth Regina, keeps the royal surface going.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon squeezer is a kitchen gadget that presses juice from a citrus fruit, so it is a kind of press.

clue.text: Poor Garth suffering negative image

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, damaged out of its usual shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unlucky Garth is in a bad way, with a gloomy picture of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' reads like sympathy for Garth, but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotograph is a photographic copy, especially of a manuscript, made as white on black, i.e. a negative print.

clue.text: Guileless unconfined weirdo making a comeback

indicators.note: taking away the boundaries of a word strips off its first and last letters
a comeback is a return, so what is left goes back the way it came

blocks.note: a deviant is someone who departs from normal behaviour, a weirdo

explanation.surface: An innocent oddball let out of confinement returns to public life.
explanation.definitionFit: Guileless describes someone without cunning or deceit, which is what an innocent, naive person is.

clue.text: Minute deception nobbles sense

indicators.note: to nobble someone is to get hold of them, so the outer word grabs the other inside it

blocks.note: a sell is informal for a hoax or swindle
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A tiny trick gets the better of common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective for tiny, but it is the unit of time. To nobble is British slang for tampering with, as with a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Smell is one of the five senses, alongside sight, hearing, taste and touch.

clue.text: Directed ICBM out to faraway place

indicators.note: directed means steered or arranged, so the letters are set into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An intercontinental missile is aimed at a distant target.
explanation.walkthrough: ICBM is an intercontinental ballistic missile, which fits the long-distance surface but is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbuctoo, the Mali city, is proverbially the remotest place imaginable, used for anywhere very far off.

clue.text: A very different matter from American revolutionary party lines

blocks.note: A is a common abbreviation for American
FARC were the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, a guerrilla group that became a party
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. lines

explanation.surface: American revolutionaries' party policies are quite another thing altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a far cry from' means something very different from another thing.

clue.text: Norman's like mother, accepting new ecclesiastical benefice

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the new letter goes inside the rest

blocks.note: comme is French for like; Norman French stands for French
a dam is the mother of an animal
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Norman resembles his mother, who takes on a new church living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' looks like a man's name; it signals French, since the Normans spoke it.
explanation.definitionFit: A commendam was a church living held in trust by a cleric until a regular incumbent was appointed, so a type of benefice.

clue.text: Titian and Trotsky perhaps inspire my memories

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside the other

blocks.note: Titian is a reddish-gold hair colour and Trotsky was a Communist, a Red
cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A Renaissance painter and a Russian revolutionary prompt someone's reminiscences.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian the painter gave his name to a red-gold hair shade, and Trotsky was a Red, so both are reds of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Records are stored accounts of the past, and memories are what a person keeps of past events.

clue.text: Right bonkers theories use persuasive language

indicators.note: bonkers means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mad conspiracy theories at least make good use of the art of persuasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhetorise is to speak as a rhetorician, using oratory to persuade.

clue.text: Synthetic substance found in college that's simmering at heart

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of British college
the central three letters of the word

explanation.surface: A man-made compound is discovered in a laboratory where things are bubbling away.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymer is a large molecule built of repeated units; plastics are polymers, the archetypal synthetic substances.

clue.text: Naked environmentalists test legal resumption of possession

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the word's outer letters are removed

blocks.note: Greens are environmental campaigners or a Green Party
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: Nude eco-protesters test the law on reclaiming property.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, re-entry is a landlord's taking back possession of a property, as when a lease is forfeited.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry in property law is the legal act of a landlord reclaiming land or premises, i.e. resuming possession.

clue.text: Central part containing black, gold and blackish-green

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the core is the central part of something
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A colour chart's middle section holds black, gold and a dark green.
explanation.walkthrough: Corbeau is French for raven, and in English names a very dark green shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Corbeau is a colour name for a dark green so deep it is nearly black.

clue.text: Uncovered partition over unnamed wooden stool

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so the word loses its outermost letters
unnamed means without a name, so the abbreviation for name, a single letter, is dropped
in a down entry, over means placed above the other piece, so it comes first

blocks.note: a screen is a movable partition
pine as an adjective means made of pine wood

explanation.surface: A bare room divider sits above an anonymous wooden stool.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name. A creepie is a Scottish word for a low three-legged stool.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect a creepie is a small low stool, such as the stool of repentance in kirk.

clue.text: Thatcher, for one, in element before terms in Foreign Office

indicators.note: terms can mean ends or limits, so only the final letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: lead is a chemical element
ere is an old word for before
the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher is in her element ahead of negotiations at the Foreign Office.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaderene was a mock-grand nickname given to Margaret Thatcher as British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaderene is a humorous term for a female leader, coined for Margaret Thatcher, who is the example the clue gives.

clue.text: Non-professional boxers, outwardly selfish, strike with shame

indicators.note: outwardly points to the outside of the word, so only its first and last letters are used

blocks.note: ABA is the Amateur Boxing Association
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Amateur fighters, selfish on the surface, deliver a blow full of disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel embarrassed or ashamed, discomfiting them.

clue.text: Manual covering grill superficially and cooker for the most part

indicators.note: superficially means only on the surface, so just the outside letters are kept
most but not all of the word is kept, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: An instruction booklet on barbecues and stoves, read only skin-deep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual' looks like a handbook, but here it is an adjective meaning of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove is a covering for the hand, and manual means relating to the hands.

clue.text: Turn to hit well-known no-shower

blocks.note: your go is your turn in a game

explanation.surface: A batsman's turn to hit gives a famous absentee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-shower' is one who doesn't show up, not one who skips the shower: Godot never arrives in Beckett's Waiting for Godot.
explanation.definitionFit: Godot is the character in Beckett's play who is awaited throughout but never turns up, the most famous absentee in drama.

clue.text: Deliver burnt vegetable

blocks.note: charred means scorched or burnt

explanation.definitionFit: Chard, or Swiss chard, is a leafy green vegetable related to beet.

clue.text: Peter and David nearly fixed deck

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

clue.text: Conservative affected by tizzy surrounding European window cleaner?

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.definitionFit: A chammy (chamois) leather is soft leather traditionally used for polishing windows, so it is an example of a window cleaner.
